scenarios.hypothesis: Two test requests intended to be semantically equivalent may receive different policy treatment after normalization or routing.
scenarios.safe_oracle: An inert controlled handler records the synthetic route and policy result for each test request.
scenarios.positive_control: The canonical synthetic representation reaches the expected inert handler under the reviewed policy.
scenarios.negative_control: An intentionally different synthetic policy class remains distinct and receives its expected result.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before any state-changing endpoint or non-test deployment is involved.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: Equivalent synthetic representations receive the same policy while intentionally distinct controls remain distinct.
scenarios.request_state_trace: Record canonical and equivalent synthetic fixtures from raw input through normalization, rewrite or mount provenance, route match, middleware order, policy attachment, and inert handler reachability.
scenarios.violated_invariant: The finding exists only if requests in the same declared semantic-equivalence class receive materially different required policy treatment before equivalent dispatch.
scenarios.false_positive_guard: Reject the case when the compared requests are intentionally different policy classes, documented semantic aliases, stale fixtures, or merely select different handlers under the same effective policy.
scenarios.evidence_upgrade: Upgrade to validated only after the first causal state divergence is identified, the changed policy attachment is proven, and a synthetic counterfactual removes the policy difference.
scenarios.neighbor_regression: After remediation, replay the equivalent pair plus an intentionally distinct neighboring class and confirm common policy for the pair while the neighbor remains intentionally distinct.

scenarios.hypothesis: A route selected through a neighboring test path may receive a different middleware sequence than the reviewed route class.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled trace records the middleware sequence and synthetic identity context without business side effects.
scenarios.positive_control: The reviewed synthetic route receives the expected middleware sequence.
scenarios.negative_control: A route outside that reviewed policy class retains its intentionally different test sequence.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if the middleware sequence cannot be observed safely in the authorized test deployment.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: All routes in the reviewed class receive the same required middleware while the distinct control class remains unchanged.
scenarios.request_state_trace: Trace the reviewed fixture through route selection and middleware partial order, recording which request representation and identity state each policy component actually consumes.
scenarios.violated_invariant: A middleware trace difference becomes security-relevant only when a required policy decision no longer governs a handler that belongs to the same reviewed route and policy class.
scenarios.false_positive_guard: Reject differences caused by intentional route-group policy, instrumentation order, short-circuit behavior that still enforces the same policy, or a handler that is not actually reachable in the inert harness.
scenarios.evidence_upgrade: Upgrade only when deterministic traces bind the ordering difference to a changed policy attachment and a synthetic counterfactual restores the expected decision without changing unrelated fixture state.
scenarios.neighbor_regression: Regression verification must preserve both the reviewed route class and a neighboring intentionally different class, proving the fix did not simply flatten all middleware behavior into one result.

scenarios.hypothesis: Identity or tenant context may be attached after a routing decision that depends on that context.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled test trace records the synthetic identity context at route and policy decision points.
scenarios.positive_control: The intended synthetic identity is bound before the reviewed policy decision.
scenarios.negative_control: A neighboring synthetic identity cannot reuse a decision made for the first identity.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before using any real user or tenant data.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: Identity context is bound before the relevant policy decision and both synthetic controls retain their expected results.
scenarios.request_state_trace: Record the synthetic principal and tenant state at every routing and policy checkpoint so the trace shows exactly when identity binding and tenant binding become authoritative inputs.
scenarios.violated_invariant: The invariant is broken only when a reviewed routing or policy decision requires principal or tenant context but is made before that required context is bound to the synthetic request state.
scenarios.false_positive_guard: Reject the case when early routing is intentionally identity-independent, when later policy correctly re-evaluates the decision, or when fixture principals differ in ways the reviewed contract says are meaningful.
scenarios.evidence_upgrade: Upgrade only after deterministic source and synthetic traces show the timing dependency, a modeled counterfactual changes only binding timing, and neighboring principal controls exclude unrelated route-state explanations.
scenarios.neighbor_regression: After remediation, verify the intended synthetic identity is bound at the required checkpoint while a neighboring synthetic identity and intentionally public control retain their documented route and policy outcomes.
